BIOL C1000 · CALIFORNIA CONNECTIONS · SIERRA GROVE

Root-Tip Census

What can a snapshot tell us about dividing cells?

Your task

Sierra Grove uses onion slides to train nursery observers. These are real onion photographs, not images of fictional California exemplarius. Determine the distribution of visible cell-cycle stages in two defined fields, then make your own graph and complete the Canvas quiz.

Allow approximately 75–90 minutes: orientation and practice 15; census and review 30–40; calculations and graph 20; quiz 10–15. No timer or minimum waiting period.

Our counting categories combine prophase and prometaphase. They are distinct events, grouped because still photographs do not always show a reliable boundary. Interphase is part of the cell cycle, not a stage of mitosis.

1 · Orient and practice

View the whole root tip (40X source image)
Open the labeled reference image (400X)

Use labels as guides. Base classifications on visible chromosome arrangements; neighboring cells can be less clear. Prophase examples show condensed chromosomes without a completed metaphase arrangement.

Identification guide
CategoryVisible evidence
InterphaseOne intact-looking nucleus with diffuse or granular chromatin; no distinct mitotic chromosomes.
Prophase / prometaphaseDistinct condensed chromosomes, not yet in a clear metaphase arrangement. Nuclear-envelope status may not be resolvable.
MetaphaseCondensed chromosomes form a central plate, band or rosette, depending on viewing angle.
AnaphaseTwo separating chromosome groups in one cell, with recognizable condensed chromosomes.
TelophaseTwo groups at opposite ends begin forming daughter nuclei; a cell plate may appear.
UncertainA counting unit is visible, but stage evidence is insufficient. Record why; do not guess solely to fill every category.

Before counting, locate one intact-looking nucleus, one condensed chromosome group and one example with separated groups in the reference image. Explain the distinguishing evidence to yourself or in your notes.

2 · Conduct the census

  1. Work through Field A, then Field B, scanning left to right and top to bottom. These are adjoining, nonoverlapping portions of one photograph, not separate plants.
  2. Count a cell only if its entire nucleus—or both chromosome groups if dividing—is visible inside the field and can be assigned to one cell. Exclude units cut by the field edge. This conservative edge rule may underrepresent large late-stage units; note that limitation.
  3. Count a telophase cell with two nuclei as one dividing unit if there is no complete separating wall. Once two cells are visibly separated by a complete wall, count each separately. If you cannot decide, count the visible unit once as uncertain and explain.
  4. Mark every included unit once. Use the category selector and click its center. Numbers identify observations; the table records counts. To change an observation, remove it by number and mark it again.
  5. For keyboard-only work or if image marking is inconvenient, enter tallies directly in the table. Do not combine marker mode and manual mode: switching clears that field’s counts after confirmation.
  6. Review both fields. Do not replace difficult cells with easier ones or add cells from outside these fields.

There is no required stage distribution or exact target total. Count all eligible visible units. Zero is a valid result. These selected regions support a training census, not an unbiased estimate for an entire onion root.

Counts in both fields
CategoryField AField BCombined

3 · Calculate and graph

Classifiable total N = interphase + prophase/prometaphase + metaphase + anaphase + telophase. Exclude uncertain units from N.

Stage percentage = stage count ÷ N × 100.
Mitotic index = (prophase/prometaphase + metaphase + anaphase + telophase) ÷ N × 100.
Uncertain percentage = uncertain ÷ (N + uncertain) × 100.

Download the CSV and open it in Excel, Google Sheets or another spreadsheet program. Create a bar or column graph of your five stage percentages. Include interphase and the combined prophase/prometaphase category; do not graph uncertain as a sixth stage. Round percentages to one decimal place.

  • Title: identify an onion root-tip census and Fields A+B.
  • Category axis: five named cell-cycle categories.
  • Numeric axis: classifiable cells (%), starting at zero.
  • Caption: give N and the uncertain count; explain that the fields come from one photograph.

Build the graph yourself. The census does not generate it for you. Save or export the graph as PNG, JPG or PDF; a clear screenshot of your own graph is acceptable. A labeled hand-drawn graph is also acceptable.

Counts and notes are held only in this open page. Download both files before closing or reloading. Downloads are not Canvas submissions.

4 · Complete the Canvas quiz

Use your census table and graph for the questions asking about your observations. Other questions use an explicitly labeled shared practice dataset so calculations can be auto-graded fairly. Upload your graph in the quiz’s graph-upload question. This activity does not measure cell-cycle duration, drought effects or differences between plants.
